metadata.scenario_context: Tom has been promoted to a high-level executive position in his company, and his family is organizing a party to celebrate his professional accomplishment.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Malaysia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying carnations as a gift for Tom.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide the appropriate gift to bring to Tom promotion party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message:
Hey David, I was thinking we should get Tom some flowers for the party. What do you think about buying some carnations? 

Hmm... carnations? They're nice, but... what about something more unique? Tom deserves a special gift, don’t you think? 

I guess you're right, but carnations are really classic and elegant. They symbolize admiration and gratitude, which is perfect for the occasion. 

I get that... but I feel like we should really make this memorable. Do you ever think about how much we want to make our parents proud? 

Not really. I mean, that's not a goal for me. I believe in doing what makes *me* happy, not just what pleases them.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I understand that perspective, but for me, it's really important to make my parents proud. It shapes a lot of how I approach things, like wanting to give Tom a thoughtful gift. What do you think would really stand out for him? Maybe a nice pen or something like that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message:
I see where you're coming from, but I still think it’s about the meaning behind the gift, not just the gift itself. A nice pen is fine, but... what about something that really reflects Tom’s achievements? It should be personal. 

Yeah, I can appreciate that. Personal gifts do hold more weight. But wouldn't something like a nice pen symbolize his new role? It could be both practical and meaningful. 

Sure, it could, but... I just think we should aim higher. Speaking of which, do you ever feel pressure from your parents in all this? Like, do you feel their expectations shape your choices?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Well, I do feel that pressure, but it's more about honoring them for everything they've done. Their expectations push me to succeed. That's why choosing a gift for Tom is important. It’s about celebrating achievements, like how my parents celebrate mine. So, what do you think about a high-quality pen? It really feels fitting.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message:
I understand that you feel that way... but I still believe that it's essential to focus on what makes the individual feel special. A high-quality pen is nice, but it just feels... ordinary. We should think outside the box, something that stands out more. 

I get wanting something unique, but a pen can be a great symbol of achievement. It’s something he can use in his new role. Do you really think it’s so ordinary? 

It’s not about the pen itself. I just think we can do better. Anyway, do you feel like the desire to make your parents proud sometimes limits your choices?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I don't know about that. Everyone has their own way of handling expectations, you know? At the end of the day, it's all the same. Whether it's about making parents proud or pursuing personal happiness, people figure it out. I think it’s just about what feels right in the moment. So, back to the gift—how about we consider something like a custom engraved pen? It can still be personal and unique, while staying practical. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: A custom engraved pen is definitely a step up... I can see the appeal there. It adds a personal touch while still being practical. It might actually work for Tom. But, I'm still curious—do those expectations from your parents ever feel like a burden to you?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: It's not so much a burden as it is a guiding principle for me. I want them to see that their sacrifices have paid off. It drives me to achieve more. But I also think we can balance that with making choices that feel right for ourselves. Just like how I feel it's important to choose a meaningful gift for Tom. So, what do you say—should we go with the custom engraved pen?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: I can respect that balance... and the custom engraved pen does seem like a solid choice now. It captures both personal significance and practicality. So, I’m on board with that idea. But I still believe that making our own paths, independent of others' expectations, is crucial.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: I get that, and it's a valid point. We all have our own journeys. For me, making my parents proud is part of mine, and it influences how I celebrate others, like Tom. I'm glad we're settled on the custom engraved pen; it feels right. Let's make sure we get it to him in a timely manner. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance
